name: Kinka
oneLiner: XNK is Kinka's gold-backed commodity token, with each token representing one troy ounce of 99.99% Japanese-brand gold bullion held with Loomis vaulting.
collateral: Each XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion held through Gold Management LLC and stored with Loomis International vaulting; issuer is Kinka (BVI) Ltd.
pegMechanism: XNK can be exchanged for physical gold through GM LLC/storage-company desks after AML/KYC; issuer docs describe a 321.5 XNK minimum for ten 1 kg bars, and secondary-market price tracks one fine troy ounce of gold.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Kinka's issuer whitepaper states that each XNK represents one troy fine ounce of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold, with bullion held at Loomis International and physical exchange through the issuer's disclosed redemption process. The reference is gold, not USD; fiat-cash is retained only as the repository's established fully-reserved commodity-token archetype, with commodityOunces carrying the operative claim measurement.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Kinka terms reserve issuer discretion over transfers and exchange and allow restrictions on Ethereum addresses; the centralized issuer and physical-gold redemption process create a direct blacklistability surface.

mintAuthority.summary: XNK uses an owner-controlled legacy mintable ERC-20; minting is not finished. The token owner is Kinka's unverified token-sale contract, whose owner is an OpenZeppelin TimelockController (1-day delay) with a 2-of-3 Gnosis Safe as sole proposer/canceller, an open executor, and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE held by the deployer EOA and the timelock itself. The Cardano deployment is an NFT-gated PlutusV3 minting policy whose authorising NFT holder is not publicly enumerable.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25625450: 13,206 bytes of unverified bytecode; function selectors match a token crowdsale (buyTokens, giveToken, sendTokens, mint, finishMinting, pause/unpause, updateLockupList, batchTransfer). owner() = 0x50EA796bCf3D178a100B1f0Ef44fAAEF64741bFE (timelock); token() = the XNK token; adminWallet = 0xE6A2356896F8a91aC473e2Be31620A235B70d8c4, saleOwnerWallet = 0xb88e8407aaf69382994234e4d64f5933a89541b8, unsaleOwnerWallet = 0x5ec59b6ea0b67b90c732e5efa7f78c441adc0838, ethManagementWallet = wallet() = 0x4777b5ffce57e453e78c0dc580f38997d194665a; paused() = true. Which of these wallets may trigger mint-path functions cannot be source-verified.

controls.label: Kinka TimelockController (sale contract owner)

sources.label: Sourcify exact match for the timelock

controls.evidence: Verified source (Sourcify exact match, verified 2024-08-08): OpenZeppelin TimelockController. At Ethereum block 25625450: getMinDelay() = 86400 seconds; hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, 0x8a4b8f479d4f1ee7b9aff581172796e1eab343b6) = true (sole proposer, also sole CANCELLER); hasRole(EXECUTOR_ROLE, 0x0) = true (open executor); hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0xE6A2356896F8a91aC473e2Be31620A235B70d8c4) = true (deployer EOA) and hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, self) = true. Complete RoleGranted/RoleRevoked log scan since deployment at block 20017160 shows no revocations and no additional grants.

controls.label: Kinka timelock proposer Safe (2-of-3)
controls.evidence: Blockscout identifies a verified GnosisSafeProxy; storage slot 0 holds masterCopy 0xd9Db270c1B5E3Bd161E8c8503c55cEABeE709552 (the canonical Gnosis Safe 1.1.1 singleton, which predates guard support). At Ethereum block 25625450: getOwners() = 3 owners (deployer EOA 0xe6a2...d8c4 plus 0xbe4681f8... and 0x35e6cbcf...); getThreshold() = 2; getModules() = empty; fallback-manager slot holds CompatibilityFallbackHandler 0xf48f2b2d2a534e402487b3ee7c18c33aec0fe5e4. This Safe is the sole PROPOSER_ROLE and CANCELLER_ROLE holder on the Kinka timelock, so every privileged mint-authority change passes its 2-of-3 quorum plus the 1-day delay.

controls.label: Kinka deployer EOA (timelock DEFAULT_ADMIN, sale adminWallet)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25625450: eth_getCode = 0x (EOA). Holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the Kinka timelock (can grant/revoke proposer and canceller roles without delay) and is the sale contract's adminWallet and one of the three proposer-Safe owners.

controls.label: XNK Cardano PlutusV3 minting policy (NFT-gated)

sources.label: Koios policy_asset_info for the XNK policy

controls.evidence: Per the 2026-07-20 bridge-route review at Cardano slot 13703132: the XNK Cardano asset (fingerprint asset1rvj40wqtucwlw6tzz4gs7080g02pm370z899m7, supply 167.0 XNK) is minted under a PlutusV3 policy whose decompiled script enforces NFT-gated policy checks; the holder of the authorising policy NFT is not enumerable from public indexer reads, so no controller address is asserted. mint_cnt 1, burn_cnt 0.

review.evidence: Wave-7 re-review at Ethereum block 25625450 resolved the previously opaque owner chain. The XNK token owner 0x2691FBB371456eaC5C5AA0082a0f53C91249c044 is Kinka's unverified token-sale contract (selector-identified crowdsale: buyTokens/giveToken/sendTokens/mint, paused() = true); its owner 0x50EA796bCf3D178a100B1f0Ef44fAAEF64741bFE is a Sourcify-verified OpenZeppelin TimelockController with getMinDelay() = 86400, sole proposer/canceller Safe 0x8a4b8f479d4f1ee7b9aff581172796e1eab343b6 (verified GnosisSafeProxy, 2-of-3, no modules, no guard), open executor, and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE held by deployer EOA 0xE6A2356896F8a91aC473e2Be31620A235B70d8c4 and the timelock itself; the complete role-event history since block 20017160 contains no revocations. The deployer EOA retains the ability to reconfigure timelock roles outside the delay, and the sale contract's operational-wallet mint permissions are not source-verifiable, so confidence stays at probable. The Cardano deployment is an NFT-gated PlutusV3 policy (slot 13703132) whose authorising NFT holder is not publicly enumerable. All three deployments are immutable with no proxy upgrade path.

reserveReview.reviewer: Grok wave-8 GROK-RESEARCH reserve re-verify; Codex T61 re-review 2026-07-31
reserveReview.rationale: Write-time re-open 2026-07-31: the 2023 whitepaper still states each XNK equals one troy fine ounce of 99.99% Japanese-brand LBMA Good Delivery gold, stored in Loomis International warehouses, with 321.5 XNK minimum physical redemption; it also describes Gold Management (GM) custody and bankruptcy isolation. The 2022 Terms of Use independently restate the one-ounce gold backing, GM/storage-company redemption path, and transfer of bullion ownership to GM LLC. The live Kinka site continues to describe vaulted gold. No published bar-level inventory, dated independent XNK-specific reserve attestation, or redemption settlement SLA was found, so composition stays a single physical-gold slice at medium risk with liquidityHorizon unknown.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Kinka whitepaper and Terms of Use physical-gold backing and redemption disclosures, re-opened 2026-07-31
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The reviewed sources identify 100% physical-gold reserve and the Loomis/Gold Management custody route but do not disclose bar-level inventory, current ounces vs circulating supply, account segregation, provider shares, or a redemption settlement time. The whitepaper states that Kinka undergoes regular audits by an independent Japanese auditing firm and that the audit scope includes Kinka and verification of its issuance, custody, and storage compliance, but the auditor is not named and no dated report or XNK-specific reserve attestation URL was located on re-open.

routes.protocol: Kinka native XNK on Cardano (PlutusV3 minting policy)
routes.reviewNote: Resolved 2026-07-20. The earlier pass queried Koios with the whole 63-character catalog string as the policy id, which returns nothing; that string is actually the full Cardano asset unit, i.e. the 56-character policy id 2c5c6ca6f993e198bc9ac859ffb624dd291ec50b4d361544bd01e3ac followed by asset name 584e4b, which decodes to ASCII 'XNK'. Queried correctly, Koios policy_asset_info returns fingerprint asset1rvj40wqtucwlw6tzz4gs7080g02pm370z899m7, total_supply 167000000 raw units (167.0 XNK at 6 decimals), mint_cnt 1, burn_cnt 0, minting tx fdda5a1033250b95fa90051212be7273fc4729bde128e6639863868d181111ae, creation_time 1745226497, and Cardano token-registry metadata pointing to the issuer site kinka-gold.com. Koios script_info shows the policy id is itself a PlutusV3 script (creation tx bca0d497b8938bdfcd8fc2c82be36ffc478ba78bf7b74899f0f742b6f13abd60) whose decompiled text references a cold reference datum and NFT-gated policy checks, so minting is authorised by holding a specific policy NFT rather than by a plain key. This is therefore an issuer-native Cardano mint, not a third-party bridge representation: no lock-and-mint or burn-and-mint linkage to the Ethereum deployment exists, and the two supplies are independent (Ethereum totalSupply was 315.0 XNK at block 25575184 on the same day). The holder of the authorising policy NFT could not be enumerated from public indexer reads, so no controllerAddress is asserted.
